title: “I’m Nobody! Who Are You?”
subtitle: 「我是無名小卒！你是誰？」艾蜜莉．狄金生的詩
source: 原創導讀；詩作依 Project Gutenberg《Poems by Emily Dickinson, Three Series》（1890–96 編輯版，公版），手稿版與生平依 Wikipedia〈Emily Dickinson〉〈I'm Nobody! Who are you?〉，2026-10-22 核對

sources.title: Poems by Emily Dickinson, Three Series, Complete, Project Gutenberg
Wikipedia: I'm Nobody! Who are you?

beginner.title: A Poet Nobody Knew
paras: “I’m nobody! Who are you? Are you nobody, too?” These are the first lines of a short poem by Emily Dickinson. The speaker is happy to be “nobody”. She thinks being famous — being “somebody” — sounds boring and tiring.
「我是無名小卒！你是誰？你也是無名小卒嗎？」這是艾蜜莉．狄金生一首短詩的開頭。詩中的說話者很高興自己是「無名小卒」。她覺得出名——當個「大人物」——聽起來又無聊又累人。

In the poem, being “somebody” is like being a frog. A frog says its name all day long to an admiring bog (a wet, muddy place). It is a funny picture. Dickinson is laughing at people who always want attention.
在這首詩裡，當「大人物」就像當一隻青蛙。青蛙整天對著一片仰慕牠的沼澤（又濕又泥濘的地方）叫自己的名字。這是個好笑的畫面。狄金生在嘲笑那些總是想要被關注的人。

Emily Dickinson lived from 1830 to 1886 in Amherst, a small town in the United States. She wrote nearly 1,800 poems, but only 10 were published while she was alive. Few people knew she was a poet. After she died, her younger sister Lavinia found the poems in her desk.
艾蜜莉．狄金生生於 1830 年，卒於 1886 年，住在美國的小鎮安默斯特。她寫了將近 1,800 首詩，但在世時只發表了 10 首。很少人知道她是詩人。她過世後，妹妹拉維妮亞在她的書桌裡發現了這些詩。

Her poems were first printed as a book in 1890. But the editors changed many of them to make them look “normal”. Dickinson used many dashes ( — ) and capital letters in strange places. In 1955, a new book showed her poems much closer to the way she wrote them.
她的詩在 1890 年首次集結成書出版。但編輯們修改了其中很多首，讓它們看起來比較「正常」。狄金生在詩裡用了很多破折號（—），也會在奇怪的地方使用大寫字母。到了 1955 年，一本新書才讓她的詩更接近她原本寫下的樣子。

Another famous poem begins: “Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul.” Hope is like a little bird inside us. It keeps singing, even in a storm, and it never asks for anything. She also wrote that no ship can take us as far as a book: “There is no frigate like a book.” Dickinson was “nobody” in her lifetime, but today she is one of America’s greatest poets.
另一首著名的詩開頭是：「希望是長著羽毛的東西／棲息在靈魂裡。」希望就像我們心裡的一隻小鳥，即使在暴風雨中也不停歌唱，而且從不索求任何東西。她也寫過，沒有一艘船能像一本書那樣帶我們走那麼遠：「沒有一艘戰艦比得上一本書。」狄金生在世時是個「無名小卒」，如今卻是美國最偉大的詩人之一。

intermediate.title: “I’m Nobody! Who Are You?”
paras: Most poems about fame celebrate it or mourn its absence. Emily Dickinson’s “I’m Nobody! Who are you?” does neither. Its speaker greets the reader as a fellow “nobody” and suggests they keep their secret, because being “somebody” sounds dreary. In just eight lines, the poem turns a common fear — being unimportant — into a kind of private freedom. The critic Harold Bloom suggested that the poem is popular because it speaks to a universal feeling of being on the outside.
大多數關於名聲的詩，若不是歌頌它，就是哀嘆得不到它。艾蜜莉．狄金生的〈我是無名小卒！你是誰？〉兩者都不是。詩中的說話者把讀者當成一個同為「無名小卒」的夥伴來問候，並提議兩人保守祕密，因為當「大人物」聽起來很沉悶。短短八行，這首詩就把一種常見的恐懼——不被重視——轉化成一種私密的自由。評論家哈洛．卜倫認為，這首詩之所以受歡迎，是因為它觸及一種普遍的感受：被排除在外。

The second stanza delivers the poem’s sharpest image. Being somebody, the speaker says, is “public, like a frog” that tells its name all day long “to an admiring bog”. The comparison is comic but pointed: the frog’s audience is only a swamp, and its message is simply its own name. Readers today often notice how well the image fits the endless self-promotion of social media.
第二節帶出了這首詩最犀利的意象。說話者說，當個大人物就像「青蛙一樣公開」，整天對著「一片仰慕牠的沼澤」報上自己的名字。這個比喻很滑稽，卻一針見血：青蛙的觀眾只是一片沼澤，牠傳達的訊息也不過是自己的名字。今天的讀者常會注意到，這個意象和社群媒體上無止盡的自我宣傳多麼契合。

Dickinson herself was, in a sense, a nobody. Born in Amherst, Massachusetts, in 1830, she wrote nearly 1,800 poems, but only 10 were published during her lifetime. Few people around her knew about her writing. After her death in 1886, her younger sister Lavinia discovered the poems in her desk. She studied at Amherst Academy for seven years and briefly attended Mount Holyoke Female Seminary before returning home.
從某種意義上說，狄金生本人就是一個無名小卒。她 1830 年生於麻薩諸塞州的安默斯特，寫了將近 1,800 首詩，但在世時只發表了 10 首。她身邊很少人知道她在寫作。1886 年她過世後，妹妹拉維妮亞在她的書桌裡發現了這些詩。她在安默斯特學院讀了七年，又在曼荷蓮女子學院短暫就讀，之後才回到家中。

When the poems were first published in 1890, the editors significantly altered them to fit the poetic conventions of the time. They smoothed out her dashes, unusual capital letters and irregular rhymes. In “I’m Nobody!”, her handwritten line “they’d advertise — you know!” became “They’d banish us, you know.” Only in 1955, when Thomas H. Johnson published a complete edition, were the poems restored closer to her original intention.
這些詩在 1890 年首次出版時，編輯們為了符合當時的詩歌慣例，對它們做了大幅修改。他們抹平了她的破折號、不尋常的大寫字母和不規則的押韻。在〈我是無名小卒！〉中，她手稿上的「他們會到處宣揚——你知道的！」被改成「他們會把我們放逐，你知道的。」直到 1955 年湯瑪斯．H．強森出版全集，這些詩才恢復到更接近她原意的樣子。

That editorial change matters. “Banish” makes the world sound cruel; “advertise” makes it sound noisy and nosy, which is exactly the poem’s point. Dickinson’s other famous lines, such as “Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul”, show the same gift for turning a large idea into a small, exact image. The poet who called herself nobody now speaks to millions of readers. Her poem about books makes a similar move: “There is no frigate like a book.”
這個編輯上的改動很重要。「放逐」讓世界聽起來很殘酷；「宣揚」則讓它聽起來吵鬧又愛管閒事——這正是這首詩的重點。狄金生的其他名句，例如「希望是長著羽毛的東西／棲息在靈魂裡」，也展現了同樣的天賦：把一個龐大的概念，轉化成一個小而精確的意象。自稱無名小卒的詩人，如今對著數百萬讀者說話。她寫書的那首詩也用了類似的手法：「沒有一艘戰艦比得上一本書。」

advanced.title: The Poetry of Being Nobody
paras: “I’m Nobody! Who are you?” opens with a question that reverses the usual logic of ambition. Rather than lamenting obscurity, the speaker treats it as a bond: finding a fellow nobody, she proposes that they keep their status secret. In the second stanza, the alternative is mocked with a single comic image. To be “Somebody” is to be “public — like a Frog”, announcing one’s name through the long summer to “an admiring Bog”. Fame, in this view, is not glory but tedious self-advertisement before an audience that cannot judge.
〈我是無名小卒！你是誰？〉以一個顛覆野心慣常邏輯的問題開場。說話者不哀嘆默默無聞，反而把它當成一種連結：找到另一個無名小卒後，她提議兩人保守自己的身分祕密。在第二節，另一種選擇被一個滑稽的意象嘲弄。當「大人物」就是「像青蛙一樣公開」，整個漫長的夏天都在對著「一片仰慕牠的沼澤」報上自己的名字。在這種觀點下，名聲不是榮耀，而是在一群無法評判的觀眾面前，乏味地自我宣傳。

The poem acquires additional irony from the circumstances of its author. Emily Dickinson, born in Amherst, Massachusetts, in 1830, was a prolific writer who produced nearly 1,800 poems, yet only 10 were published during her lifetime. Few in her circle were aware of the scale of her work. After her death in 1886, her younger sister Lavinia discovered the poems in her desk, and what had been a private practice became, posthumously, one of the most significant bodies of poetry in American literature.
這首詩因作者的處境而多了一層反諷。1830 年生於麻薩諸塞州安默斯特的艾蜜莉．狄金生，是一位多產的作家，寫了將近 1,800 首詩，但在世時只發表了 10 首。她身邊的人很少知道她作品的規模。1886 年她過世後，妹妹拉維妮亞在她的書桌裡發現了這些詩，原本私密的寫作，在她身後成為美國文學中最重要的詩歌作品之一。

Her path to readers, however, involved considerable distortion. When a selection appeared in 1890, edited by Thomas Wentworth Higginson and Mabel Loomis Todd, the poems were significantly altered to fit prevailing conventions. Her distinctive dashes and capitals were regularised, and some words were replaced. The second line of “I’m Nobody!” lost its dashes, and the manuscript’s “they’d advertise — you know!” became “They’d banish us, you know.” The substitution changes the poem’s meaning: banishment implies punishment by an authority, whereas advertisement implies exposure by gossip — precisely the publicity the speaker wishes to avoid.

然而，她走向讀者的路上，經歷了相當大的扭曲。1890 年由湯瑪斯．溫特沃斯．希金森和梅布爾．盧米斯．托德編選出版時，這些詩為了符合當時盛行的慣例而被大幅修改。她獨特的破折號和大寫字母被規範化，有些字詞也被替換。〈我是無名小卒！〉的第二行失去了破折號，而手稿上的「他們會到處宣揚——你知道的！」變成了「他們會把我們放逐，你知道的。」這個替換改變了詩的意義：放逐意味著權威的懲罰，宣揚則意味著被閒話曝光——而這正是說話者想避開的公眾目光。

Only in 1955, when Thomas H. Johnson published a complete edition, were the poems presented nearly as Dickinson had left them: untitled, numbered, strewn with dashes and irregularly capitalised, often elliptical in their language. The restored texts revealed a poet of great formal daring. Dickinson frequently worked within the familiar ballad stanza, yet she unsettled it with slant rhyme and abrupt compression, as if testing how much meaning a short line could hold.
直到 1955 年湯瑪斯．H．強森出版全集，這些詩才幾乎以狄金生留下的樣子呈現：沒有標題、只有編號、遍布破折號、大寫不規則，語言往往省略跳躍。恢復後的文本，揭示了一位在形式上極為大膽的詩人。狄金生常在熟悉的民謠詩節中寫作，卻以斜韻和突然的壓縮打亂它，彷彿在測試一行短詩能承載多少意義。

That capacity for compression is visible in her best-known lines. “Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul” turns an abstraction into a small bird that sings “the tune without the words” and, the speaker notes, has never asked “a crumb” in return. The poems endure partly because they are brief enough to memorise and strange enough to reward rereading. They also offer a reminder relevant to an age of constant visibility: a life lived largely out of public view can still produce work of lasting public value. Elsewhere she made the same move with reading itself: “There is no frigate like a book / To take us lands away.”

這種壓縮的能力，在她最知名的詩句中清晰可見。「希望是長著羽毛的東西／棲息在靈魂裡」把一個抽象概念變成一隻小鳥，牠唱著「沒有歌詞的曲調」，而說話者指出，牠從未索求過「一粒麵包屑」作為回報。這些詩能流傳下來，部分是因為它們短到可以背誦，又奇特到值得一讀再讀。它們也提供了一個與這個時時刻刻都在曝光的時代息息相關的提醒：一段大多遠離公眾目光的人生，仍能創造出具有長久公共價值的作品。在別處，她也對閱讀本身用了同樣的手法：「沒有一艘戰艦比得上一本書／能帶我們遠赴他鄉。」

phrases.usage: 放句首或句中，表示部分同意。
phrases.example: In a sense, we are all learners.
phrases.writing: S + was, in a sense, + N

phrases.meaning: 抹平、修整（smooth out 的過去式）

He helped me and asked for nothing in return.

patterns.frame: Most A do X or Y. B does neither.

patterns.example: Most poems about fame celebrate it or mourn its absence. Emily Dickinson’s poem does neither.

quote.text: Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul, / And sings the tune without the words, / And never stops at all.
quote.author: Emily Dickinson

beginner.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: Why editors added dashes to Dickinson’s poems.
How frogs call out their names in a muddy bog.
A poet who called herself “nobody” and later became famous.
How Lavinia Dickinson became a famous poet.
beginner.evidence: Dickinson was “nobody” in her lifetime, but today she is one of America’s greatest poets.
beginner.why: 全文：生前沒沒無聞、寫「我是無名小卒」的詩人，如今成為美國最偉大的詩人之一。
traps: 正反顛倒：編輯是把她的破折號拿掉。
字面誤讀：青蛙只是詩裡的比喻。
張冠李戴：Lavinia 是發現詩稿的妹妹。

beginner.q: What does the word “bog” mean in the second paragraph?
options: A wet, muddy place.
A large crowd of people.
A small green frog.
A famous person’s name.
beginner.evidence: to an admiring bog (a wet, muddy place)
beginner.why: 括號直接解釋：潮濕泥濘的地方。
traps: 過度推論：沼澤在詩中像觀眾，但字面意思不是人群。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：青蛙是對著沼澤叫的那一方。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：青蛙喊的是自己的名字。

beginner.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Dickinson’s older brother found the poems in her desk.
Dickinson published nearly 1,800 poems during her lifetime.
Her poems were first printed as a book in 1955.
Only 10 of Dickinson’s poems were published while she was alive.
beginner.evidence: only 10 were published while she was alive
traps: 張冠李戴：發現詩稿的是妹妹 Lavinia。
數字錯位：寫了約 1,800 首，生前只發表 10 首。
數字錯位：第一本詩集是 1890 年，1955 年是較接近原貌的新版。

beginner.q: What does the poem “Hope is the thing with feathers” suggest about hope?
options: It flies away from us whenever a storm comes.
It stays with us in hard times and asks for nothing.
It must be paid for with something very valuable.
It belongs only to people who are famous.
beginner.evidence: It keeps singing, even in a storm, and it never asks for anything.
beginner.why: 最後一段：希望像小鳥，暴風中仍唱歌，從不要求回報。
traps: 正反顛倒：它在暴風中仍唱歌。
正反顛倒：它從不要求任何東西。
捏造：詩人本身就是「無名小卒」。

intermediate.q: Which of the following best states the main idea of the passage?
options: Social media was invented because of Dickinson’s frog image.
Dickinson wanted to become as famous as possible during her life.
Thomas H. Johnson wrote “I’m Nobody! Who are you?”.
Dickinson’s poem treats being unknown as a freedom, and her own life matched it.
intermediate.evidence: the poem turns a common fear — being unimportant — into a kind of private freedom
intermediate.why: 第一段點題，第三段說她本人也是「無名小卒」。
traps: 因果顛倒：讀者只是覺得這個意象很像社群媒體。
正反顛倒：詩中說當名人很無趣。
張冠李戴：Johnson 是 1955 年版的編者。

intermediate.q: What does “dreary” in the first paragraph most likely mean?
options: Exciting and new.
Dull and tiring.
Secret and hidden.
Cruel and unfair.
intermediate.why: 詩人覺得當名人很「沉悶乏味」，就像青蛙整天報自己名字。
traps: 正反顛倒：她覺得出名並不有趣。
原文字眼、錯誤關係：保守秘密是她對讀者的提議。
張冠李戴：「殘酷」是 banish 這個改字帶來的感覺。

intermediate.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Dickinson studied at Amherst Academy for two years.
The 1890 editors kept all of Dickinson’s dashes.
The 1890 editors changed “they’d advertise” to “They’d banish us”.
Johnson’s complete edition appeared in 1890.
intermediate.evidence: her handwritten line “they’d advertise — you know!” became “They’d banish us, you know.”
traps: 數字錯位：原文說讀了七年。
正反顛倒：編輯把破折號抹平了。
數字錯位：Johnson 的全集在 1955 年。

intermediate.q: Why does the author say “That editorial change matters”?
options: “Banish” and “advertise” give the poem different meanings.
The editors misspelled Dickinson’s name.
The new word made the poem much longer.
Dickinson asked the editors to change it.
intermediate.evidence: “Banish” makes the world sound cruel; “advertise” makes it sound noisy and nosy
intermediate.why: 最後一段：banish 讓世界顯得殘酷，advertise 則是吵鬧、愛打聽，後者才是詩的重點。
traps: 捏造：問題在改字，不在拼名字。
捏造：只換了一個詞，長度不是重點。
時序錯置：1890 年詩集出版時她已過世。

advanced.q: What is the main purpose of the passage?
options: To show how her life and editors shaped the poem’s view of fame.
To argue that Dickinson’s poems should be rewritten in modern English.
To describe the ballad stanza used in English folk songs.
To prove that Higginson was a better poet than Dickinson.
advanced.evidence: The poem acquires additional irony from the circumstances of its author.
advanced.why: 全文：詩的主題、作者生平的反諷，以及編輯如何改動她的詩。
traps: 捏造：作者讚賞的是恢復原貌的版本。
以偏概全：民謠詩節只是說明她的形式。
捏造：Higginson 是編者，作者批評他的改動。

advanced.q: What does “posthumously” in the second paragraph mean?
options: Written in secret by hand.
Before the writer was born.
After the writer’s death.
Edited by a famous critic.
advanced.evidence: After her death in 1886, her younger sister Lavinia discovered the poems in her desk, and what had been a private practice became, posthumously, one of the most significant bodies of poetry
advanced.why: 同一句：她死後詩稿才被發現並出版。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：手寫稿是詩的形式，不是這個字的意思。
正反顛倒：她 1830 年出生。
張冠李戴：編者是另一件事。

advanced.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: The 1955 edition gave every poem a title.
Higginson and Todd edited the 1890 selection.
Dickinson never used the familiar ballad stanza.
Dickinson’s capitals were kept exactly in 1890.
advanced.evidence: edited by Thomas Wentworth Higginson and Mabel Loomis Todd
traps: 正反顛倒：1955 年版保留她「沒有標題、以數字編號」的原樣。
正反顛倒：她常用民謠詩節，只是加以打破。
正反顛倒：大寫字母被規範化了。

advanced.q: Why does the change from “advertise” to “banish” alter the poem’s meaning?
options: Banishment makes the poem rhyme more regularly.
Banishment sounds more modern than advertisement.
Advertisement was a word Dickinson never used.
Banishment implies punishment, while advertisement implies gossip and exposure.
advanced.evidence: banishment implies punishment by an authority, whereas advertisement implies exposure by gossip
traps: 捏造：作者分析的是意義，不是押韻。
捏造：問題在意思，不在新舊。
正反顛倒：advertise 正是她手稿裡的字。

reflections: Would you rather be a “somebody” or a “nobody”? Use the frog image in your answer.
Write your own two-line poem in Dickinson’s style that turns a big idea (such as fear, love or time) into a small image.

videos.title: The Poetry of Emily Dickinson: Crash Course Literature #8
videos.desc: John Green explores Dickinson’s life, dashes and ideas. (10 min)
videos.zh: 約翰．葛林談狄金生的人生、破折號與思想。（10 分鐘）
videos.question: What does the video say about Dickinson’s dashes? Why might editors have removed them?

paras: “I’m Nobody! Who are you?” opens with a question that turns the usual logic of ambition upside down. Rather than complaining about being unknown, the speaker treats it as a bond: finding a fellow nobody, she suggests that they keep their status secret. In the second stanza, the alternative is mocked with a single comic image. To be “Somebody” is to be public, like a frog announcing its own name all summer long to “an admiring Bog” (a wet, muddy place).
〈我是無名小卒！你是誰？〉以一個問題開場，把一般的野心邏輯整個顛倒過來。說話者不抱怨沒沒無聞，反而把它當成一種連結：遇到另一個無名小卒，她提議兩人保守這個秘密。在第二節，另一種人生被一個滑稽的畫面嘲笑：當個「大人物」，就是公開示人，像一隻整個夏天對著「仰慕的沼澤」（潮濕泥濘的地方）報自己名字的青蛙。

The poem gains extra irony from its author’s life. Born in Amherst, Massachusetts, in 1830, Emily Dickinson wrote nearly 1,800 poems, yet only 10 were published while she was alive. Few people around her knew how much she had written. After her death in 1886, her younger sister Lavinia discovered the poems in her desk, and what had been a private habit became one of the most important bodies of poetry in American literature.
這首詩因作者的生平而更添諷刺。1830 年生於麻州安默斯特的艾蜜莉．狄金生，寫了將近 1,800 首詩，生前卻只發表了 10 首。她身邊很少有人知道她寫了多少。1886 年她去世後，妹妹拉薇妮雅在她的書桌裡發現了這些詩，原本私密的習慣，變成了美國文學中最重要的詩作之一。

Her path to readers, however, involved serious distortion. When a selection appeared in 1890, edited by Thomas Wentworth Higginson and Mabel Loomis Todd, the poems were heavily changed to fit the fashions of the time. Her dashes and capital letters were smoothed out, and some words were replaced. In “I’m Nobody!”, her handwritten line “they’d advertise — you know!” became “They’d banish us, you know.” The change matters: banishment suggests punishment by an authority, whereas advertising suggests exposure by gossip, which is exactly the publicity the speaker wants to avoid.
然而，她的詩送到讀者手中的過程中，經過了嚴重的扭曲。1890 年由希金森和陶德編選的詩集出版時，詩被大幅修改，以符合當時的風尚：她的破折號和大寫字母被抹平，有些字被換掉。在〈我是無名小卒！〉裡，她手寫的「他們會到處宣揚——你知道的！」被改成「他們會把我們放逐，你知道的。」這個改動很關鍵：放逐意味著權威的懲罰，宣揚則意味著被八卦曝光——而後者正是說話者想避開的名聲。

Not until 1955, when Thomas H. Johnson published a complete edition, were the poems presented nearly as Dickinson had left them: untitled, numbered, full of dashes and unusual capitals. The restored texts revealed a poet of great daring. She often worked within a familiar song-like stanza, yet she unsettled it with imperfect rhymes and sudden compression, as if testing how much meaning a short line could hold.
直到 1955 年強森出版全集，這些詩才幾乎以狄金生留下的樣子呈現：沒有標題、以數字編號、滿是破折號和不尋常的大寫字母。恢復原貌的詩作，展現出一位非常大膽的詩人。她常在熟悉、像歌謠般的詩節裡寫作，卻用不完全的押韻和突然的壓縮打破它，彷彿在測試一行短詩能承載多少意義。

It is this gift for compression that her best-known lines show. “Hope is the thing with feathers / That perches in the soul” turns an abstract idea into a small bird that keeps singing and has never asked for “a crumb” in return. Elsewhere she made the same move with reading: “There is no frigate like a book.” The poems last partly because they are short enough to memorise and strange enough to reward rereading. They also offer a reminder for an age of constant visibility: a life lived largely out of public view can still produce work of lasting public value.
她最有名的詩句，展現的正是這種壓縮的天分。「希望是長著羽毛的東西／棲息在靈魂裡」把一個抽象的概念，變成一隻不停歌唱、從沒討過「一點麵包屑」的小鳥。在別處，她對閱讀也做了同樣的事：「沒有一艘戰艦比得上一本書。」這些詩之所以流傳，部分是因為它們短到能背下來，又奇特到值得一讀再讀。它們也給這個時時被看見的時代一個提醒：一個大多不在公眾視線下的人生，仍能創造出具有長久公共價值的作品。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: How to write a poem without any dashes.
How frogs announce their names in muddy places.
Why Higginson was a better poet than Dickinson.
How a poem about being unknown matches its author’s life and history.
questions.evidence: The poem gains extra irony from its author’s life.
questions.why: 全文：詩的內容、作者生前沒沒無聞，以及詩作被編輯改動又恢復的歷史。
traps: 正反顛倒：破折號正是她的特色。
字面誤讀：青蛙只是詩中的比喻。
捏造：希金森是編者，作者批評他的改動。

questions.q: What does “it” in “treats it as a bond” in the first paragraph refer to?
options: The usual logic of ambition.
Being unknown.
The second stanza.
A comic image.
questions.evidence: Rather than complaining about being unknown
questions.why: 前面的 being unknown：沒沒無聞。
traps: 原文字眼、錯誤關係：野心的邏輯是被顛倒的對象。
時序錯置：第二節在後面。
時序錯置：滑稽的畫面在下一句。

questions.q: Which of the following is true according to the passage?
options: Lavinia was Dickinson’s older sister.
Dickinson published nearly 1,800 poems while she was alive.
Only 10 of Dickinson’s poems were published in her lifetime.
Johnson’s complete edition appeared in 1890.
questions.evidence: yet only 10 were published while she was alive
traps: 正反顛倒：拉薇妮雅是妹妹。
數字錯位：寫了約 1,800 首，生前只發表 10 首。
數字錯位：1955 年。

questions.q: What can be inferred about the change from “advertise” to “banish”?
options: It weakened the poem’s point about publicity and gossip.
It made the poem rhyme more perfectly.
It was the change Dickinson herself wanted.
It made the poem shorter and easier to remember.
questions.evidence: which is exactly the publicity the speaker wants to avoid
questions.why: 「宣揚」才扣合詩對曝光、八卦的嘲諷；換成「放逐」削弱了這個重點。
traps: 捏造：作者分析的是意思，不是押韻。
正反顛倒：她手寫的是 advertise。
捏造：文中沒提長短。

mixed.prompt: Dickinson’s poems were heavily [47] by her first editors, and they were not restored nearly to her original form until a complete [48] appeared in 1955.
mixed.why: 第一格出自第三段 were heavily changed（被動）；第二格出自第四段 a complete edition。

mixed.q: Which of the following are stated in the passage? Choose ALL that apply.
options: Dickinson was born in Amherst, Massachusetts.
Lavinia found the poems in Dickinson’s desk.
The 1890 editors kept all of her dashes.
Johnson’s 1955 edition left the poems untitled and numbered.
Dickinson wrote that a ship is better than a book.
The 1890 selection was edited by Johnson.
mixed.why: A、B 第二段；D 第四段。C 正反顛倒（破折號被抹平）；E 正反顛倒（沒有戰艦比得上書）；F 張冠李戴（1890 年是希金森和陶德）。

mixed.q: What was Dickinson’s original word that the editors replaced with “banish”?
